<thought>We have a molecular ion at m/z 100.0524, matching the exact monoisotopic mass of C₅H₈O₂ (DBE = 2). The ¹³C NMR shows five distinct carbons: two sp² carbons (≈136 ppm and 117 ppm), one oxygen‑bearing carbon (≈70 ppm), one methoxy‑like carbon (≈54 ppm), and one aliphatic carbon (≈44 ppm). This pattern is consistent with an alkene (two DBE) bearing an ether/alkoxy group, such as methyl vinyl ether (CH₂=CH‑O‑CH₃) but that formula is C₃H₆O. To reach C₅H₈O₂ we need an additional –CH₂–O– fragment. A plausible structure is **methyl 2‑methoxy‑prop-2‑ene** (also called methyl isopropenyl ether), SMILES: `C=C(C)OC`. This molecule has C₅H₈O₂, two sp² carbons (≈136 ppm, 117 ppm), an O‑attached tertiary carbon (≈70 ppm), a methoxy carbon (≈54 ppm), and a methyl carbon (≈44 ppm). The predicted spectra would match the observed data.** 

<final_answer>C=C(C)OC</final_answer>
